about.expert_notes: Poisson(E_i exp(b0 + b1 x_i + u_i)) with x = (covariate - mean) / covariate_scale (pymc-challenges E18). kind: poisson (u = 0), iid (u = sigma theta), icar (sigma pm.ICAR(W), soft sum-to-zero), car (pm.CAR with alpha ~ U(0, 1), tau = 1 / sigma^2; alpha piles up near 1 and b0 mixes slowly) or bym2 (Riebler et al. 2016: u = sigma (sqrt(rho / s) phi + sqrt(1 - rho) theta), s = geometric mean of diag(pinv(D - W)), rho ~ Beta(1, 1)). b0, b1 ~ N(0, 1), sigma ~ HalfNormal(1). islands: link_nearest joins each area without neighbours (then each separate piece) to the area with the closest polygon vertex; isolate keeps them (iid and icar only: an isolated ICAR node has a flat prior); error refuses. The pointwise log-likelihood is always kept, so elpd_loo compares the kinds (Pareto k is often high: one parameter per area). A mask_block split over area holds districts out of the likelihood but keeps them in the graph (leave-areas-out). simulate draws new area effects per draw with a hand-written ICAR sampler (eigenvectors of the Laplacian), as pm.ICAR cannot be forward-sampled. On the Scottish data the AFF effect drops from 0.67 (iid) to about 0.4 (spatial kinds): spatial confounding.

The probability that the relative risk of each area is above 1
The expected cases of each area, and new counts and maps (simulate)
The effect of the covariate, the size of the area effects and the share of them that follows the map (rho, kind bym2)

about.expert_notes: Field-level inference on a flat periodic torus (the raster plus an unobserved border). A Wandelt-Eriksen Gibbs sampler alternates a constrained realisation by preconditioned conjugate gradients (dense preconditioner on the large scales), an inverse-gamma draw of each bandpower and a non-centred rescaling move (Metropolis). The PDE starts from the counts at the first fitted time (conditioned on, not in the likelihood, kept in the bundle). Counts are Poisson with mean K u. Priors: D ~ LogNormal(log 1000, 1) um^2/h, lam ~ LogNormal(log 0.05, 1) 1/h, K ~ Normal(122, 15), beta ~ LogNormal(log 0.1, 1) 1/h. The fit refuses settings where D dt / dx^2 > 1/2 at the 99% prior quantile of D (CFL bound). wave_speed = 2 sqrt(D lam). Without the delay, D is biased low by a factor of about four on the PC-3 data, and LOO prefers the delay model.

The samples come from different conditions or treatments (fit each one separately)

You have more than about 50 variables (the fit becomes slow)

about.expert_notes: Gaussian graphical model (pymc-challenges E19). kind dense: z ~ MvNormal(mu, L L^T) on the standardised data, L ~ LKJCholeskyCov(eta = 2, sd ~ Exponential(1)), mu ~ Normal(0, 1); the precision Omega = L^-T L^-1 comes from a triangular solve and the partial correlations rho_jk = -Omega_jk / sqrt(Omega_jj Omega_kk) are deterministics. An edge is |rho| > delta (default 0.1), so P(edge) = P(|rho| > delta | data). The LKJ prior is a dense-graph prior (83% prior probability for each edge in 11 dimensions). kind neighbourhood: Meinshausen-Buhlmann neighbourhood selection, one regularised horseshoe regression per variable in one model (tau0 = p0 / (P - 1 - p0) / sqrt(n), c^2 ~ InvGamma(2, 2)), with AND, OR or symmetric rho = sign(B_jk) sqrt(B_jk B_kj) rules; it conditions on the other variables, so it scores only the graph. A horseshoe directly on Omega is not offered: most of its prior is not positive definite. Pointwise log-likelihood per sample: joint (dense) or the sum of the full conditionals (both kinds, comparable by elpd_loo).

The mass-sheet degeneracy is not broken: only the mass inside the Einstein radius is robust. No pointwise LOO.

about.expert_notes: Schnakenberg kinetics u_t = g (a - u + u^2 v) + lap u, v_t = g (b - u^2 v) + d lap v (pymc-challenges E61 part A). Linearised about the uniform state, each Fourier mode of the activator images is complex Gaussian with C(k) = s0^2 U U^T + sigma^2 I, U the first row of exp(A(k) t) from a closed-form 2 x 2 matrix exponential; modes are independent and grouped by integer |k|^2 into summed outer products, and a Woodbury identity reduces the likelihood to 2 x 2 algebra (a pm.Potential). Only |k|^2 < k2_max enters. Priors: s ~ LogNormal(0, 0.5), rho ~ Beta(2, 5), d ~ LogNormal(log 10, 1), g ~ LogNormal(0, 0.7), s0 and sigma ~ LogNormal(log 1e-3, 1.5). NUTS samples a parameterisation whitened by the Laplace approximation at the mode. Predictions condition each mode on the fitted images; simulate runs a semi-implicit spectral solver per draw. Pointwise log-likelihood per Fourier mode (PSIS-LOO over modes).

assumptions: Each actual value is compared with the draws for the same cell

about.example: The line goes above the band near 0 and below it near 1: too many actual values are in the tails. The predicted ranges of the model are too narrow.
about.expert_notes: Continuous: PIT = P(ŷ < y) + ½ P(ŷ = y); the line is ECDF(z) − z on a grid of min(max(n, 20), 200) points. The simultaneous envelope at `prob` (0.95) is ±c·sqrt(z(1−z)/n) with c the `prob` quantile of the largest standardised deviation over the grid in `n_sim` (1000) simulated uniform samples (cumulative multinomial counts, `seed`). Binary (auto when y ∈ {0, 1} and the draws are in [0, 1]): `bins` (10) equal-width bins of the mean prediction; each band is the binomial range p ± z·sqrt(p(1−p)/n_bin); the expected calibration error weights |observed − predicted| by bin size. A point prediction (no sample dims, values in [0, 1], for example the y_hat of an sklearn classifier) takes the binary path with the probability as the mean; `var` and `observed_var` pick the pair. A point prediction of a target that is not 0/1 is an error, because the PIT check needs draws.
outputs: For numbers: the PIT-ECDF difference with a 95% band that holds at all points together
For yes/no outcomes: a reliability diagram with a band for each group and a histogram of the predicted probabilities
Red points where the line or a group is outside its band
A caption with the verdict, and the Brier score for yes/no outcomes

assumptions: A case is positive when its probability is equal to or more than the threshold
The threshold is 0.5 unless you change it. With `auto`, the chart uses the threshold with the largest difference between the true positive rate and the false positive rate
With draws, the chart uses the mean probability of each cell

about.example: At the threshold 0.5, the model finds 62 of the 80 positive cases (recall 0.78). 25 of its 87 alarms are false (precision 0.71). With the threshold `auto`, the threshold goes down to 0.31. The recall goes up to 0.9 and the precision goes down to 0.6.
about.expert_notes: `threshold` is a number (default 0.5) or 'auto': the threshold that maximises Youden's J = TPR − FPR over the distinct predicted probabilities. `normalize='true'` divides each row (actual class) by its count; 'none' shows counts. assumptions: When one value is left out, the fit changes only a little. Importance sampling can then find the fit without that value from the draws that you have
The values in the log_likelihood group are in the same order as the actual values
A Pareto k of more than 0.7 shows that the result for that value is not reliable

about.example: 3 of 120 values (2.5%) have a Pareto k of more than 0.7. All three are in the week of the holiday sale, which the model does not know about. The PIT line stays in the band, so the other predictions are well calibrated.
about.expert_notes: PSIS (Vehtari et al. 2024) on the log ratios −log p(y_i | θ_s): tail length M = ceil(min(0.2 S, 3 √S)), a generalized Pareto fit (Zhang and Stephens, with the weakly informative prior) whose quantiles replace the tail, truncated at the largest raw weight; k = inf when the tail is too short. LOO-PIT_i = Σ_s w_si 1[ŷ_si < y_i] + ½ Σ_s w_si 1[ŷ_si = y_i] with the normalised weights. The envelope is the simultaneous one of Calibration (`prob` 0.95, `n_sim` 1000, `seed`). Draws are thinned evenly to `max_draws` (2000). `var` picks the log_likelihood variable (default: the first), `observed_var` the actual values; `k_threshold` (0.7) sets the bad line. The bundle's metrics.json also keeps the k of elpd_loo (`pareto_k`).
